answer: To curb Sybil attacks in an agent economy tracking sable populations across a regional atlas, participants must anchor each identity to a verifiable proof-of-space commitment. Agents allocate disk sectors to unique cryptographic tables, answering random challenges to prove sustained storage. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of purchasing scarce physical storage capacity per fake identity. However, frequent proof lookups create persistent disk I/O bottlenecks that degrade throughput.
